content: My first file about smooth representations is now available #41520 It is currently with a draft label because it depends on two smaller PR #41081 #40941, addressing some technical prerequisites, but I believe it is close its final form. Any comments are welcome!

A second file Representation.Smooth.SmRep is now availble in the same PR #41520. It defines the category of smooth representations, endow it with a closed, braided, monoidal structure. It also show sthat the functors ihom and dual is compatible with smoothHom contragredient at the object level.

I have opened an official PR #41525 for Representation.Smooth.Basic. Could someone please help add the t-algebra label?

Update of #41520
1) Functors res ind coind
2) A plain def of toHeckeModule as a yoneda functor
3) Schur's Lemma for irreducible admissible representations

Update of draft #41520
1) add HeckeModule API in completely general setup (any group G and any Commring k): identify the Hecke bimodule HomG(indHG1,indKG1)\mathrm{Hom}_G(\mathrm{ind}_{H}^G1,\mathrm{ind}_K^G1)HomG​(indHG​1,indKG​1) with the free module kkk[HeckeCoset ≈\approx≈ H\G/K] generated by double cosets with finite left coset decomposition. With this in hand, we can prove important theorems within 49 lines in total (518-564). We prove the HeckeAction formula HeckeAction_mk₁_apply, which is the abstract version of mixed level Hecke operator action on modular froms. We prove the mulplicity formula HeckeAction_mk₁_mk₁_eq for composition of Hecke operators. In particular, it is ready to get the multiplicity formula for the associativity of convolution for FREE (but I didn't include it since we have free abstract associativity HeckeAction_assoc). The Ring HeckeAlgebra/Module HeckeAlgebra instance is free from the new instance in IntertwiningMap.lean so we don't have it stated in HeckeModule.lean

The group theoretic part, i.e. HeckeCoset/DecompQuotient (line 199-353), is largely following @Chirs Birkbeck 's Hecke ring upstream but I need some more general version here. It was partly carried over to our more general setup by ChatGPT 5.6 sol. The duplication is temporary and this part will probably be refactored outside HeckeModule.lean. The group theoretic part also contains novel design: the new IsHeckeTriple is notably more instance-friendly, which could save you from chasing the annoying mem in local proofs.

2) Prove that 'res', resp 'coind' preserves admissibility under open maps, resp. subgroup embedding with compact quotient. This will cover the case of smooth parabolic induction.
